title: Escape speed
target: Explain escape in an ideal gravitational-energy model.
criteria: Distinguish escape speed from circular-orbit speed.
Name neglected effects in the ideal calculation.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: With U = 0 at infinity, an object starts with U = −72 J. What minimum initial K allows it to reach infinity with zero final speed in the ideal model?
options: 0 J
cpa.guide: Minimum escape has total E = 0, requiring K = −U = 72 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A probe starts with K = 95 J and U = −65 J, then coasts without losses. What is its kinetic energy at infinity?
options: 0 J
cpa.guide: Total energy is +30 J; U approaches zero, leaving K = 30 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: At the same radius, how does ideal escape speed compare with circular-orbit speed?
options: They are identical.
Escape speed is √2 times circular speed.
Circular speed is always zero.
Escape speed is half circular speed.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A spacecraft is in a stable circular orbit with no thrust. Which claim is correct?
options: Any nonzero altitude means escape.
It must be moving at escape speed.
It is continually falling around the planet and has not necessarily escaped.
Circular orbit means gravity is zero.
cpa.guide: Circular motion is bound by gravity; escape requires sufficient total energy.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Which assumption belongs to the simple escape-speed model?
options: Negligible atmospheric drag and no later propulsion.
The launch speed can be zero for any planet.
Mass grows continuously as the craft rises.
Gravity becomes zero immediately above the surface.
cpa.guide: The basic energy model neglects drag and further engine work.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A launch has exactly the ideal minimum escape energy but encounters drag. What can be concluded?
options: The planet must lose all gravity.
The ideal result no longer guarantees escape because drag removes mechanical energy.
Drag always increases orbital energy.
Escape is still guaranteed regardless of losses.
cpa.guide: With losses, initial energy must account for the energy removed as well.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
